title: kb_backlog_write refuses every call when a settings file has no permissions key, though it holds no deny rule
goal: a project settings file that holds no permissions or deny key is read as holding no deny rule, and a file that cannot be parsed still denies every call, so kb_backlog_write is not blocked by a settings file that says nothing about Bash

run:
import sys, os, json, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbcommon, kb_mcp
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(os.path.join(T, ".claude"))
json.dump({"env": {"A": "1"}}, open(os.path.join(T, ".claude", "settings.local.json"), "w"))
kbcommon.HOME = type(kbcommon.HOME)(T)
hit = kb_mcp.bash_denied("python3 _tools/backlog.py release ST-aaaaaaaa")
assert hit is None, ("a valid settings file with no permissions key denies the call", hit)
